jobs.title: Senior Bio Information Analyst - UAV & Environmental Tech
jobs.description:
Lead Auckland Council's environmental UAV programme and support best-practice aerial data collection
Combine ecology, geospatial analysis and emerging technologies to drive better environmental outcomes
Mentor pilots, champion innovation and shape the future of environmental data capability

He angitūtanga: The opportunity

Auckland Council's Environmental Services department has an opportunity for a Senior Bio Information Analyst to join Bio Information Team.

With a passion and understanding of ecosystem services, to take on both spatial analysis and Senior Remote Pilot duties, including those delegated from our Chief Pilot, this role sits at the intersection of ecology, geospatial technology, UAV operations and environmental innovation.

You'll play a key role in how environmental information is captured, analysed and transformed into insights that support biodiversity protection, ecological monitoring and environmental decision-making across Tāmaki Makaurau.

We are CAA certified and maintain a high standard of UAV best practice in our ecological survey, including thermal night flights; you’ll be comfortable leading by example, and helping maintain the high standards expected within our CAA-certified programme

As a senior member of the team, you'll also contribute to our Enabling Tools programme, identifying opportunities to use emerging technologies, automation and digital solutions to improve environmental outcomes and organisational capability along with mentoring pilots across the department.

Please note:
The official title for this position is S enior Bio Information Analyst
. We've included UAV & Environmental Tech
in the advertised title to reflect the primary focus areas of this vacancy.

Day-to-day you could expect to:

Support and enhance Auckland Council's Environmental Services UAV programme, including delegated Senior Remote Pilot responsibilities.
Deliver expert GIS, spatial analysis and environmental information management advice across a range of environmental initiatives.
Undertake and support UAV-based ecological surveys, mapping and environmental monitoring activities.
Mentor and support UAV pilots, contributing to capability development and best-practice operations across the department.
Identify and implement innovative digital, imagery and data solutions that improve environmental outcomes and organisational capability.

He kōrero mōu: About you

This role requires significant experience in environmental information, spatial analysis, GIS or a related natural science field, alongside the confidence to provide technical leadership and specialist advice.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working where ecology and technology come together, someone who can go beyond simply managing data. You'll be naturally curious, solutions-focused and motivated by finding new ways to collect, analyse and apply environmental information.

Ideally, you'll have experience operating UAVs to best-practice standards and be certified to 102, along with experience in IoT and image processing.

Our must-haves:

A relevant Bachelor’s degree in an environmental discipline, natural sciences or computer science, together with 7+ years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of natural sciences, ideally New Zealand ecology, and experience working with environmental information.
Proven experience developing and implementing information, database, geospatial or data-support solutions.
Advanced capability in ESRI ArcGIS/spatial mapping and/or database design and management, with strong Microsoft Office skills and experience using relevant ecological analysis software.
A full NZ driver’s licence, along with the communication, initiative, relationship-building and resilience to operate confidently in a complex, collaborative environment.

Nice to haves:

A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
Experience with ecological surveys and assessing the significance of natural areas.
Knowledge of SQL database design and functionality in an environmental management context.
Experience specifically across biodiversity, biosecurity or geological information.
Experience mentoring other analysts or leading technical work, projects or information initiatives.

Most importantly, we’re looking for someone with the drive to make environmental information useful. You’ll need to be comfortable taking ownership, solving problems where there isn’t always an obvious answer, influencing others and confidently providing advice to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You’ll also bring an appreciation of Te Ao Māori and tikanga, and a willingness to continue developing your confidence and capability in te reo Māori and our Treaty responsiveness journey.

Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou: What we offer

Auckland Council is the largest local government council across Oceania, serving over 1.7 million people and contributing towards making Tāmaki Makaurau a world-class city.

We offer a range of employee benefits and proudly support flexible working options where possible.

You’ll have access to a range of fantastic Auckland Council benefits, EAP services, an Oranga Day and discounted Leisure Centre membership and a range of other partnership discounts! View a snapshot of some of our employee benefits here :

This Is a Senior Technical Position And Is The Third Step In The Series Of Four. This Posting Is Used To Fill Multiple Positions Throughout The City Of Tacoma And Tacoma Public Utilities. Vacancies May Occur Within The Following Teams

City of Tacoma IT GIS
City of Tacoma Environment & Public Works GIS
Tacoma Water GIS
Tacoma Power GIS

The Tacoma Public Utilities' and City of Tacoma are looking for an experienced GIS Analyst who is passionate about creating innovative solutions to solve business problems. Our ideal candidate is capable and motivated to assist in the administration, design, architecture, configuration, and implementation of our GIS Enterprise environment.

The successful candidate should possess extensive knowledge and experience architecting, configuring, implementing, and maintaining ArcGIS Enterprise environments (ArcGIS Portal, ArcGIS Servers, ArcGIS Data Store). Knowledge regarding other GIS solutions used at the City, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS, ArcGIS Experience Builder, Web Appbuilder, ArcGIS Monitor, VertiGIS Studio, VertiGIS Analytics, ArcGIS Monitor, Python, FME and ESRI Enterprise Databases are also desirable.

Responsibilities Include

System Administration

Lead the administration, design, architecture, configuration, and implementation of solutions that leverage the City's Web GIS platforms, including: ArcGIS Enterprise deployment, monitoring, and administration, security, manage certificates, ArcGIS licensing (Desktop and Enterprise), performance/system monitoring (ArcGIS Monitor, Geocortex Analytics), geodatabase/data store administration, system patching, automating and reporting system uptime
Perform daily administration of Enterprise Geodatabases and GIS applications
Extract, compare, analyze, and develop solutions to keep systems in alignment
Track and troubleshoot system issues proactively using ArcGIS Monitor, VertiGIS Analytics or other GIS system monitoring tools

Data Management

Test software and database upgrades, perform end-user training, and troubleshoot system issues to determine solutions, resolve, and follow up
Develop and implement procedures for data design, processing, quality control, automation, documentation,metadata, maintenance and ETLs (Extract, Transform and Load)

Application Development

Address customer's information needs by designing, developing, testing, deploying and supporting GIS Applications using a variety of tools and development languages

Bachelor degree in Computer Science or related field, including Technology, Engineering, and Geography; AND

GIS Professional Certification (GISP), ESRI Technical Certifications or any other GIS Certification Program

Expert knowledge of specialized technologies, such as applications, tools, systems, and/or databases.
Knowledge of principles and concepts of total quality management and problem-solving methods.
Understanding of data and system security and other similar technical processes approaches.
Expertise in Cloud GIS, asset management, and platform integrations is highly desirable.

Skill in applying advanced technical knowledge to evaluate and resolve complex tasks such as planning and directing projects, conducting capacity planning, coordinating or facilitating the installation of complex systems, hardware, software, application interfaces or applications.

jobs.title: Environmental Manager 2 - Stormwater Specialist
jobs.description:
Work for Indiana

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About Indiana Department Of Environmental Management (IDEM)

Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

Role Overview

This position exists within the Office of Water Quality and will be stationed in the Indianapolis Office of the Indiana Department of Environmental Management. However, based on the candidate selected alternate locations may be considered.

The position is responsible for administering stormwater regulations in an efficient and consistent manner. The primary function of this position is to administer the stormwater program, which includes a multidisciplinary approach to stormwater management, erosion and sediment control, and pollution prevention. Responsibilities include permitting industrial and construction sites and contributing to program development. Responsibilities also include but are not limited reviewing stormwater pollution prevention plans and conducting regulatory inspections for construction sites and industrial facilities and audits of local Municipal Separate Storm Sewer Systems (MS4s).

This position requires a valid IN driver's license.

Salary

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $53,222.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Serves as an environmental expert and provides guidance to regulated communities, government officials, attorneys and staff responsible for a variety of programs and program elements.
Project Management: Performs project management duties to ensure effective and timely management of program area needs, attends meetings, and responds to telephone calls, e-mails, etc., as required. Acts as a technical point-of-contact for assigned programs administering environmental programs which may include, but not limited to, environmental media sampling, data analysis, technical writing, work plan and report preparation, technical reviews, etc.
Permits: Researches state and federal guidance, laws, and regulations related to permits. Contacts applicants to request additional information to process applications, when necessary. Responds to comments from applicants, defends permit terms and conditions, and interacts with permittees to resolve permitting issues. Attends and participates in public meetings and hearings regarding permit actions throughout Indiana and/or appears in legal appeals of permit actions.
Inspection: Conducts surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, reads plans, interprets findings, and cites appropriate violations of state and federal regulations. Provides technical and regulatory guidance to the regulated community in their assigned geographic area.
Enforcement & Compliance: Uses all compliance, enforcement tools, and resources available to ensure that regulated sources return to compliance with state and federal laws, regulations, and standards in a timely manner.
Support Services: Works to support the various programs in assigned agency in multiple capacities.
Sampling: Assists with the preparation of sampling and analysis work plans. Conducts field work as necessary following agency/section Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for assigned sites.
Technical Analysis & Testing: Conducts technical analysis and/or provides technical insights to assess environmental impacts with goals to meet state and national regulations.
Outreach Coordination: Communicates effectively with responsible parties, consultants, and/or their representatives, affected stakeholders, and interested parties such as citizens, public officials, and interest groups in a courteous and professional manner regarding permits, laws, questions, and program-related inquiries.
Essential functions of this position require travel on most workdays to inspect, audit, examine, survey, or investigate clients, customers, or other regulated entities and write reports at various sites depending on business needs. Employee reports to the agency’s office for occasional meetings or events. Number and timing of work hours may vary daily or weekly to accommodate operational needs and staffing concerns at the client’s or customer’s worksite, minimize expenditures for repeated visits to complete the work, and allocate resources to complete assigned work effectively.

The job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

This position is exempt from overtime compensation for additional work hours which may be required to complete essential functions or other assigned work. Exempt employees may work more than 75 hours in a pay period without additional compensation and must report a minimum of 75 hours per pay period of work hours and/or paid leave taken to receive their base biweekly salary.

What You'll Need For Success

Individuals in this role should minimally be able to articulate or demonstrate the following:

Broad knowledge of theories, environmental protection principles and practices, specialty area, and program area.
Thorough knowledge of chemistry, biology, hydrology, mathematics, engineering, and other environmental sciences as they relate to program area.
Thorough knowledge of soil, water, air sampling, laboratory analysis and interpretation as it relates to program area.
Ability to conduct surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, read plans, interpret findings, and make recommendations.
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
Ability to effectively interact and orally communicate with parties with diverse levels of environmental expertise particularly for purposes of meetings, hearings, and negotiating critically sensitive issues.
Ability to interpret and apply legal terminology and practices, and the ability to apply these in a variety of conditions and situations.

A degree is not required. However, at least five (5) years of environmental or environmental public health experience applying the outlined knowledge, skills, and abilities in a similar role may be considered.

Individuals should have the ability to perform essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Environmental Graphics Officer is responsible for designing, evaluating, and managing high-quality signages, wayfinding systems, spatial graphic displays, and property enhancement set-ups across the integrated resort. Reporting to the Environmental Graphics leadership, the primary objective of this role is to elevate guest navigation, support brand consistency, and maintain the aesthetic and structural integrity of all environmental graphics through precision design, site assessments, and strict adherence to Service Level Agreements (SLAs). The position operates within the limits of established brand guidelines, safety standards, material and fabrication budgets, and departmental project management protocols, requiring technical accuracy, creative initiative, and flexibility to meet project deadlines.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Environmental Graphic & Spatial Design

Design comprehensive property signages, wayfinding systems, and graphic artwork in alignment with the resort’s brand identity and team scope.
Develop conceptual and production designs for temporary and permanent spatial installations, including promotional booths, VIP lounges, stage set-ups, construction hoardings/board-ups, and property improvement elements.
Produce precise layout specifications, scale drawings, and detailed plans reflecting accurate dimensions for all proposed signage and graphic installations.

Site Inspection & Technical Assessment

Conduct initial site ocular inspections for proposed projects to assess physical space dimensions, structural requirements, and material suitability.
Perform daily site ocular inspections for ongoing and installed projects to monitor the physical condition, functionality, and visual appeal of signages under the team's accountability.
Apply technical understanding of floor plans, elevations, section plans, and architectural terminology to ensure seamless integration of designs with existing resort structures.

Fabrication & Material Coordination

Evaluate and select appropriate building and construction materials suitable for various environmental conditions across the property.
Oversee and guide signage fabrication processes, ensuring technical standards are met for components such as backlit displays, LED adboxes, lightboxes, and architectural signage.

Project & Workflow Management

Manage incoming project job orders to ensure strict adherence to agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and project timelines.
Evaluate workflow processes, organize project task lists, and prioritize design deliverables to optimize team efficiency.
Report real-time project status, operational risks, and design bottlenecks to superiors, ensuring timely escalation and necessary approvals.

Stakeholder Engagement & Administrative Support

Participate in and present design concepts, technical proposals, and project deliberations during stakeholder meetings.
Draft professional email communications, design briefs, and presentation materials for internal and external project collaborators.
Provide ongoing technical and administrative support to team leadership to streamline overall department operations and daily workflows.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Civil/Structural Engineering, Fine Arts, Graphic Design, or an equivalent field of study.
Work Experience:
Minimum of 2–3 years of hands-on experience in environmental graphics, signage design, wayfinding, or spatial/exhibition set-up design, ideally within large-scale commercial, hospitality, or resort properties.
Technical & Software Proficiency:

Advanced proficiency in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software and graphic layout programs, including Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, CorelDraw, and relevant 2D/3D drafting tools.
Strong ability to read, interpret, and generate technical layout plans, floor plans, structural elevations, and section diagrams.
Fabrication & Material Knowledge:

Solid understanding of architectural/building materials, visual display components, and fabrication techniques for lighted signs, LED adboxes, lightboxes, and structural installations.
Communication & Soft Skills:

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with proven confidence in delivering technical presentations, writing project briefs, and collaborating across teams.
Strong aesthetic judgment, creative imagination, and attention to detail.

Position Description

JOB DESCRIPTION

Nevada Gold Mines is looking for an Environmental Specialist to join our Environmental Team at the Phoenix Mine. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining and improving the site’s environmental management systems, with a primary focus on ISO 14001, Cority, environmental document control, and GIS.

The successful candidate will work closely with Environmental, Operations, Engineering, and other site departments to ensure environmental information is accurate, accessible, properly documented, and maintained in accordance with regulatory and company requirements.

This is an excellent opportunity for an individual who enjoys working with environmental data and systems while also having the opportunity to support field activities and continuous improvement initiatives.

Responsibilities

Support the ongoing implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the site’s ISO 14001 Environmental Management System.
Maintain ISO 14001 documentation, records, procedures, forms, and associated environmental management system information.
Support internal and external ISO 14001 audits, including preparation of documentation and evidence.
Track audit findings, corrective actions, opportunities for improvement, and associated action plans.
Assist with maintaining environmental objectives, targets, programs, and performance metrics.
Support environmental aspect and impact assessments and evaluation of compliance processes.
Assist with Management of Change (MOC) processes from an environmental perspective.
Track environmental management system action items and ensure documentation is completed and maintained.
Support employee awareness and training related to ISO 14001 and environmental management system requirements.
Serve as a key user and administrator/support resource for the site's Cority environmental management system.
Maintain the Environmental Department's document control system.
Ensure environmental procedures, plans, work instructions, forms, permits, reports, and records are properly controlled and current.
Maintain and update environmental GIS databases, maps, and spatial data.
Develop maps and figures to support environmental permitting, compliance, reclamation, monitoring, and reporting activities.
Manage environmental spatial data, including sampling locations, monitoring points, reclamation areas, disturbance areas, infrastructure, permits, and other environmental features.
Support users with data entry, system questions, and troubleshooting.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Manages budgets, including the budget for external ISO audits.
Coordinates with supply chain personnel to procure contractor and consultant services, as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree preferred
Experience with compliance systems and ISO 14001 preferred
Experience with PowerPoint, Publisher, Word, and Excel required
Three to five years in a mining industry setting preferred
Experience in Environmental compliance programs preferred
Excellent verbal, written, presentation and interpersonal skills required
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously required

About Us

Our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business. We are committed to partnering with our host countries and communities to transform their natural resources into tangible benefits and mutual prosperity.

Barrick is a leading global mining, exploration and development company. With one of the largest portfolios of world-class and life-long gold and copper assets in the industry - including six of the world's Tier One gold mines - Barrick's operations an projects span 18 countries and five continents. Barrick is also the largest gold producer in the United States. We create real, long-term value for all stakeholders through responsible mining, strong partnerships, and a disciplined approach to growth. Barrick shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "B" and on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol "ABX".

Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) is a joint venture between Barrick (61.5%) and Newmont (38.5%) that combined our significant assets across Nevada in 2019 to create the single largest gold-producing complex in the world. NGM produces approximately 3.5 million ounces of gold a year. The massive mining operation comprises eight mines along with their associated infrastructure and processing facilities and hosts three of Barrick’s Tier One assets: Carlin, Cortez, and Turquoise Ridge. At NGM, our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and owning the best assets, with the best people, to deliver sustainable returns for our owners and partners.
